title: Adaptive slot preemption and per-tenant concurrency floor
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add per-tenant concurrency floor to guarantee minimal throughput; implement adaptive slot preemption with grace windows and smooth backoff; expose new telemetry metrics for preemption rates and concurrency-floor utilization.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated capacity customers need predictable minimum throughput even when the cluster is under pressure. Today we only have proportional soft reservations and opportunistic preemption which can cause sudden throughput drops for small tenants when large tenants spike. This PR introduces a per-tenant concurrency floor (soft-guarantee) plus an adaptive slot preemption mechanism that free slots from over-provisioned tenants with minimal disruption.

Design summary:
- Concurrency floor: each tenant can configure a small non-evictable floor expressed in concurrent slots (floor_slots). The runtime guarantees these slots are preserved unless a tenant explicitly relaxes them. Floors are enforced with a fast-path check in allocator.
- Adaptive preemption: when cluster pressure rises, allocator computes a target reclaim amount and identifies candidate slots using weighted age+utilization scoring. Instead of immediate hard eviction we perform soft preemptions (SIG_PREEMPT equivalent) that signal running requests to checkpoint or extend deadlines, and then evict after a grace window. Grace windows are proportional to request age with a max cap.
- Smooth throttle transitions: add a one-way exponential backoff for tenants that are being reduced; helps avoid oscillation when load is bursty.
- Telemetry: new metrics emitted per-tenant: preemptions_total, preemption_latency_ms_histogram, floor_utilization_p50/p90/p99. Also added an allocator event stream for debugging.

- 5d3a7c9: preempt: implement soft preempt signal and grace window handler
- 8b9e4c0: scoring: age+utilization candidate selector and reclaim policy
- d2c6a11: api: tenant config schema, validation, and admin CLI flags

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/allocator/allocator.go (main logic, ~220 additions)
- runtime/allocator/preempt_handler.go (soft preempt signalling, ~120 additions)
- api/tenant/config.proto (schema changes)
- cli/admin/tenant_set_floor.go (admin CLI)
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go (new metrics and registration)
- tests/integration/preempt-grace-window.test (scenario tests)
- docs/config/concurrency-floor.md (user docs + migration)
- dashboards/tenant-floor-overview.json (dashboard wiring)

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_concurrency_floor` (default off).
- Stage 1: enable in internal canary with small set of tenants. Monitor floor_utilization and preemptions_total.
- Stage 2: opt-in for select Dedicated customers via support.
- Stage 3: enable by default with conservative default floors and soft preemption thresholds.

Notes on backward compatibility and risk:
- Floors are opt-in and do not change default allocation.
- Soft preemption relies on request-level cooperative handling (best-effort): long-running opaque workloads may still be forcibly evicted after grace window. We document this and provide guidance for tuning.
- Risk: new telemetry could slightly increase cardinality; metrics are tagged sparsely and default sampling is applied.

Relation to existing work: this complements proportional reservation work (ENG-1122) but differs by offering an explicit tenant-configured minimum and a coordinated preemption signal to smooth evictions.

review_comments: Luis Ramirez (2026-02-11): Overall design looks reasonable. Two concerns: 1) how do we ensure floors don't starve small tenants when cluster is near capacity? 2) scoring function seems O(n) per allocation - will this be a perf hit?

Maya Chen (2026-02-11): For (1) floors are intended to be small and opt-in; we added a cluster-level floor-cap so total floors can't exceed a configurable percentage. For (2) we memoize candidate scores and only recompute on state changes - added bench in allocator_test.
Priya Nair (2026-02-13): Please add a short circuit in preempt_handler when grace window is exceeded to avoid double signals. Also add a unit test for preemption latency histogram buckets.
Maya Chen (2026-02-14): Addressed both; added preempt_handler.shortCircuit and histogram unit test (commit 0e3f1b5).
Elliot Graves (2026-02-15): CI showed intermittent flake in integration test (race on tenant shutdown). We should add a small jitter before final eviction to reduce races.
Maya Chen (2026-02-16): Added jitter of up to 50ms before final eviction; reran integration tests locally and in CI.
